name: security-warehouse-export-publication-review
intent: Warehouse query/export identity and destination publication authority
artifacts: Query principal, row/column policies, export job configuration, destination credentials and artifact audience.
trace: Follow the requester approved dataset/projection into an asynchronous export and the final readable destination, including user-selected storage paths.
experiment: Use owned synthetic tables and export destinations; compare rightful export with a restricted field, tenant or destination selection.
disproof: Permission to run a public aggregate is not permission to export private rows; job acceptance alone does not show leaked bytes.
repair: Constrain data projection and destination authority, preserving intended export and denied unauthorized publication.
branch_decisions: Separate query permission, export/job identity and destination reader rights. A service account can legitimately write an export where its caller cannot directly write, provided destination selection and result entitlement are constrained. Verify one owned synthetic result and exact destination ACL; a completed query job does not establish public delivery.
operational_method: Select one actual warehouse export engine and retain query principal, row/column policy evaluation, job/service identity, export destination and final reader ACL. Trace whether projection and tenant filters apply before the service writes the artifact, and whether caller-controlled destinations widen its audience. A generic storage-writing worker stub cannot establish a warehouse-specific policy bypass. Compare an owned restricted projection with a permitted export and inspect delivered bytes, not just job success.
